MARK2012 LibWizard left panels
==============================

Paste each slide’s code into its left panel (Source view), then select Save Changes. The tip and source boxes are part of the code, so no Text Blocks are needed.
Right-panel codes are in mark2012-embed-codes.txt. Quiz questions are in mark2012-quiz.txt.

========== 1. Welcome ==========

<h3 style="border-bottom:4px solid #ffe000; padding-bottom:6px">Welcome</h3><p><strong>Need more room?</strong> Select <img alt="the collapse button" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="height:22px; width:30px; vertical-align:-6px" /> next to <strong>Menu</strong> above to hide this panel. Select the arrow again to bring it back.</p><p>Thanks for opening this tutorial. It’s here to help you find research for <strong>MARK2012 Marketing Fundamentals</strong>. It isn’t built around one assessment. The skills here work for any marketing topic you research at UNSW.</p><p>By completing this tutorial, you’ll learn to</p><ul><li><strong>Identify</strong> the key concepts in your assessment question</li><li><strong>Discover</strong> scholarly, industry and company information using Library databases</li><li><strong>Evaluate</strong> sources for relevance, currency, reliability and accuracy</li><li><strong>Use responsibly</strong> AI tools and the information you apply to your work</li></ul><p>Your progress shows in the black bar at the top of each activity. Each activity earns you a badge. Select <strong>Research log</strong> to see the searches you build and save them for later.</p><p><a href="https://info-skills-lab.github.io/library-activities/marketing-research.html?part=1" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the welcome activity in a new window</a></p><div style="background:#d9edf7; border:1px solid #bce8f1; border-radius:4px; color:#1f4e66; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:24px; width:24px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Google and AI?</strong> Fine for getting started. Always check the source, then continue in Library databases.</p></div>

========== 2. Library website ==========

<h3 style="border-bottom:4px solid #ffe000; padding-bottom:6px">Library website</h3><p>Everything about the Library and its services is on the Library website. The live website is on the right.</p><h4>What to do</h4><ol><li>Hover over <strong>Services</strong> in the top menu.</li><li>Find the services that support your studies at UNSW, such as <strong>Student workshops and events</strong> and <strong>Library Peer Mentors</strong>.</li><li>To find journal articles and other research materials, type your search terms into the search bar and run a search.</li><li>Select <strong>Next slide</strong> once you have run your search.</li></ol><p><a href="https://www.library.unsw.edu.au/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the Library website in a new window</a></p><div style="background:#d9edf7; border:1px solid #bce8f1; border-radius:4px; color:#1f4e66; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:24px; width:24px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Tip:</strong> Not sure what to search? Try plant based milk.</p></div>

========== 3. Library collection ==========

<h3 style="border-bottom:4px solid #ffe000; padding-bottom:6px">Library collection</h3><p>The Library collection searches across books, eBooks, journal articles and more. Once you have run a search, use the filters on the left of the results to refine what you find.</p><ul><li><strong>Dates</strong> to find more current results</li><li><strong>Topics</strong> to locate research on a more specific aspect of your search</li><li><strong>Resource types</strong> to locate specific formats such as eBooks and journal articles</li></ul><p>The Library collection also has an AI discovery tool called <strong>Research Assistant</strong>. Sign in, ask your question in plain English and it finds results relevant to your search.</p><h4>What to do</h4><ol><li>Type your search terms into the search bar on the right and run a search.</li><li>Set a filter under <strong>Dates</strong>, <strong>Topics</strong> or <strong>Resource types</strong>.</li><li>Select <strong>Research Assistant</strong> and ask the same question in plain English.</li></ol><p><a href="https://www.library.unsw.edu.au/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the Library website in a new window</a></p><div style="background:#d9edf7; border:1px solid #bce8f1; border-radius:4px; color:#1f4e66; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:24px; width:24px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Tip:</strong> Research Assistant works from abstracts and record details only, and it doesn’t include news. Use it to get started, then check the sources it gives you.</p></div><div style="background:#f5f5f5; border:1px solid #e3e3e3; border-radius:4px; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; font-size:0.9em; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:22px; width:22px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Source:</strong> UNSW Library, <a href="https://unswlibrary.libanswers.com/faq/278453" target="_blank" rel="noopener">What’s Library collection Research Assistant?</a></p></div>

========== 4. Breaking down the question ==========

<h3 style="border-bottom:4px solid #ffe000; padding-bottom:6px">Breaking down the question</h3><p>Every research question has its key parts. Breaking them down helps you understand the question and turns it into keywords you can search using databases, search engines and AI tools.</p><p>Words for the same idea join with <strong>OR</strong>, which broadens your results. For example, element* OR component* finds results with either word, or both.</p><p>Different ideas join with <strong>AND</strong>, which narrows your results. For example, "marketing strategy" AND "marketing plan" only finds results with both phrases.</p><h4>What to do</h4><ol><li>In <strong>1 Break down the question</strong>, choose a tag, then select the words it fits. Select <strong>Check</strong>.</li><li>In <strong>2 Build your search</strong>, spin each dial and select <strong>Add</strong> to choose your words.</li><li>Add more than one word on a dial to include synonyms.</li><li>Select <strong>+ Add a dial</strong> for your own idea.</li></ol><p><a href="https://info-skills-lab.github.io/library-activities/marketing-research.html?part=4" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the breaking down the question activity in a new window</a></p><div style="background:#d9edf7; border:1px solid #bce8f1; border-radius:4px; color:#1f4e66; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:24px; width:24px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Tip:</strong> An asterisk finds different word endings, so element* finds element and elements. This is called truncation. Quotation marks keep words together as a phrase, such as "marketing plan".</p></div><div style="background:#f5f5f5; border:1px solid #e3e3e3; border-radius:4px; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; font-size:0.9em; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:22px; width:22px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Source:</strong> UNSW Library, <a href="https://subjectguides.library.unsw.edu.au/search-skills/question" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Search skills, breaking down your question</a>.</p></div>

========== 5. Library subject guides ==========

<h3 style="border-bottom:4px solid #ffe000; padding-bottom:6px">Library subject guides</h3><p>Subject guides bring together the key databases and resources for your area of study. The Business subject guide lists the core databases for business research, with a page for marketing.</p><p>Different questions need different sources. Knowing which database to start with saves you time.</p><h4>What to do</h4><ol><li>On the right, scroll through the <strong>Core databases</strong> for business.</li><li>Select the <strong>Marketing</strong> tab to see the databases for marketing.</li><li>Find <strong>Business Source Premier</strong> and <strong>IBISWorld</strong>. You’ll use both in the next slides.</li></ol><p><a href="https://subjectguides.library.unsw.edu.au/business/core-databases" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the Business subject guide in a new window</a></p><div style="background:#d9edf7; border:1px solid #bce8f1; border-radius:4px; color:#1f4e66; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:24px; width:24px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Tip:</strong> Each database in the guide has a short description. Read it to check what the database covers before you search.</p></div>

========== 6. IBISWorld ==========

<h3 style="border-bottom:4px solid #ffe000; padding-bottom:6px">IBISWorld</h3><p>IBISWorld publishes industry reports for Australia and other markets. Each report covers how an industry is performing, its products and markets, the competition and the major companies in it.</p><p>Industries aren’t always named the way you’d search for them. A search for soy milk leads to the report <strong>Soy and Almond Milk Production in Australia</strong>.</p><h4>What to do</h4><ol><li>In <strong>1 Find the report</strong>, type soy milk and select <strong>Search</strong>, then choose the report that fits.</li><li>In <strong>2 Find the chapter</strong>, read each research need and select the chapter that meets it.</li><li>Select <strong>Open IBISWorld</strong> to find the real report.</li></ol><p><a href="https://info-skills-lab.github.io/library-activities/marketing-research.html?part=6" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the IBISWorld activity in a new window</a></p><div style="background:#d9edf7; border:1px solid #bce8f1; border-radius:4px; color:#1f4e66; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:24px; width:24px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Tip:</strong> Check the date of an industry report and use the most recent one. Industries change quickly, so older reports may be out of date.</p></div>

========== 7. Business Source Premier ==========

<h3 style="border-bottom:4px solid #ffe000; padding-bottom:6px">Business Source Premier</h3><p>Business Source Premier is a scholarly business database covering most areas of business research. Alongside peer-reviewed articles, it holds company and industry reports, conference papers, news and much more.</p><p>Consider using it to find research on</p><ul><li>why consumers choose plant-based milk</li><li>how brands position dairy alternatives</li><li>marketing strategies in the food and beverage industry</li></ul><h4>What to do</h4><ol><li>In <strong>1 Advanced search</strong>, check your search, set the filters and select <strong>Search</strong>.</li><li>Select <strong>Run it in Business Source Premier</strong> and set the same filters on the real results page.</li><li>In <strong>2 Ask a question</strong>, try the plain-English search or build your own question, then select <strong>Search</strong>.</li></ol><p><a href="https://info-skills-lab.github.io/library-activities/marketing-research.html?part=7" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the Business Source Premier activity in a new window</a></p><div style="background:#d9edf7; border:1px solid #bce8f1; border-radius:4px; color:#1f4e66; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:24px; width:24px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Tip:</strong> Peer-reviewed articles are checked by experts in the field before publication, which makes them a credible source for your research. <a href="https://subjectguides.library.unsw.edu.au/search-skills/academic-sources#s-lg-box-wrapper-27185313" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Learn more about peer review</a></p></div>

========== 8. Consumer marketing scenarios ==========

<h3 style="border-bottom:4px solid #ffe000; padding-bottom:6px">Consumer marketing scenarios</h3><p>In marketing, you’ll often start with a scenario and not a set question. The first step is the same. Pick out the key ideas, then turn them into a search.</p><p>Each key idea becomes a line in your search. Synonyms join with <strong>OR</strong>, and the lines join with <strong>AND</strong>.</p><h4>What to do</h4><ol><li>Choose a scenario on the right.</li><li>Select the words in the scenario that are key ideas, then select <strong>Check</strong>.</li><li>Read the search it builds, then select <strong>Run it in Business Source Premier</strong>.</li></ol><p>Your search saves to your Research log automatically.</p><p><a href="https://info-skills-lab.github.io/library-activities/marketing-research.html?part=8" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the consumer marketing scenarios activity in a new window</a></p><div style="background:#d9edf7; border:1px solid #bce8f1; border-radius:4px; color:#1f4e66; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:24px; width:24px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Tip:</strong> Too few results? Add a synonym with OR. Too many? Add another key idea with AND.</p></div>

========== 9. Evaluating sources ==========

<h3 style="border-bottom:4px solid #ffe000; padding-bottom:6px">Evaluating sources</h3><p>It’s always important to evaluate the information you find for your assessment. Make sure it’s relevant to your needs, current, especially if you’re researching recent developments, comes from a reliable source, and presents the facts accurately.</p><p>The CRAAP test is a quick way to check</p><ul><li><strong>Currency</strong> When was it published, and is it up to date for your topic?</li><li><strong>Relevance</strong> Does it relate to your question?</li><li><strong>Authority</strong> Who wrote or published it, and are they an expert?</li><li><strong>Accuracy</strong> Is it supported by evidence you can check?</li><li><strong>Purpose</strong> Why does it exist? To inform, sell or persuade?</li></ul><h4>What to do</h4><ol><li>Read each source on the right.</li><li>Pick the part of the CRAAP test it fails.</li></ol><p><a href="https://info-skills-lab.github.io/library-activities/marketing-research.html?part=9" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the evaluating sources activity in a new window</a></p><div style="background:#d9edf7; border:1px solid #bce8f1; border-radius:4px; color:#1f4e66; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:24px; width:24px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Tip:</strong> Find out more about selecting academic sources in the Library’s <a href="https://subjectguides.library.unsw.edu.au/search-skills/academic-sources" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Search skills guide</a>.</p></div><div style="background:#f5f5f5; border:1px solid #e3e3e3; border-radius:4px; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; font-size:0.9em; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:22px; width:22px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Source:</strong> UNSW Library, Academic sources. The CRAAP test was created by Sarah Blakeslee and the librarians at Meriam Library, California State University, Chico, licensed under CC BY 4.0.</p></div>

========== 10. Using AI responsibly ==========

<h3 style="border-bottom:4px solid #ffe000; padding-bottom:6px">Using AI responsibly</h3><p>Generative AI tools can help you get started, for example by explaining a topic or suggesting keywords. But you are responsible for what you hand in. <strong>Always check your course outline first, as each course and assessment may have different rules on using AI.</strong></p><p>Treat AI like any other source you find online, and be sure to critically evaluate its outputs. AI can produce information that is incorrect or made up, known as hallucinations, and this extends to references too. Its responses also reflect the data it was trained on, which can contain bias, and general tools like ChatGPT and Copilot are less likely to draw on peer-reviewed research.</p><h4>What to do</h4><ol><li>In <strong>1 AI at UNSW</strong>, decide whether each action is a do or a don’t.</li><li>In <strong>2 Check the output</strong>, select each numbered part of the AI answer, starting with 1, and choose the check it needs.</li></ol><p><a href="https://info-skills-lab.github.io/library-activities/marketing-research.html?part=10" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the using AI responsibly activity in a new window</a></p><div style="background:#d9edf7; border:1px solid #bce8f1; border-radius:4px; color:#1f4e66; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:24px; width:24px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Tip:</strong> Look beyond the tool. Check the sources an AI answer cites, and the sources it might be missing. The <a href="https://subjectguides.library.unsw.edu.au/search-skills/sift" target="_blank" rel="noopener">SIFT method</a> can help.</p></div><div style="background:#f5f5f5; border:1px solid #e3e3e3; border-radius:4px; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; font-size:0.9em; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:22px; width:22px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Source:</strong> UNSW, <em>Responsible use of generative AI tools: a guide for UNSW students</em>; UNSW, <a href="https://www.unsw.edu.au/student/managing-your-studies/academic-skills-support/toolkit/ai" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Using Artificial Intelligence (AI) in university</a>; UNSW Library, <a href="https://subjectguides.library.unsw.edu.au/search-skills/ai-critically" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Using AI critically</a>.</p></div>

========== 11. Build a business research prompt ==========

<h3 style="border-bottom:4px solid #ffe000; padding-bottom:6px">Build a business research prompt</h3><p>AI tools can help you scope a topic, summarise an industry and brainstorm search terms, but they can also invent figures and references. A useful formula for a prompt is <strong>Intent + Context + Instruction</strong>. For industry research, tell the tool which sources to use, such as industry reports, and ask it to show where each fact comes from. Always check your course’s rules on using AI.</p><h4>What to do</h4><ol><li>Fill in the five steps on the right. Type your own words or select a suggestion. Each number turns into a tick when done.</li><li>Select <strong>Copy prompt</strong> to use your prompt in an AI tool.</li><li>Check every figure and source in the AI response using the Library’s core business databases.</li></ol><p><a href="https://info-skills-lab.github.io/library-activities/marketing-research.html?part=11" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the business research prompt activity in a new window</a></p><div style="background:#d9edf7; border:1px solid #bce8f1; border-radius:4px; color:#1f4e66; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:24px; width:24px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Tip:</strong> Ask for the author, date and link for every source, so you can find and check the original.</p></div>
